reviews.rationale: Sequential comparison of selected SEC exhibit rows shows a mixed picture rather than a clean directional signal. Supporting the constructive side: GAAP net interest income rose sequentially, and the increase in net interest income exceeded the increase in interest expense, so the pre-provision revenue base expanded; non-interest income also rose; and GAAP common-attributable net income increased, with the tax line essentially unchanged. Supporting the credit-quality side: classified assets, classified loans on accrual, and special mention loans all declined, repossessed assets fell, the combined nonperforming-asset ratio eased, and the annualized net charge-off rate was unchanged. Opposing evidence: the provision for credit losses rose materially, so net interest income after provision grew far less than net interest income; the allowance for loan losses and total allowance for credit losses both rose; nonaccrual loans increased; and loans past due 30 to 89 days still accruing increased. The non-interest expense increase was of a similar order to the non-interest income increase, so the expense-side contribution to the earnings improvement is not established. The Q2 and Q3 non-interest income components carry different labels and scope, so the non-interest income increase cannot be attributed to a comparable origination-and-sale gain line. All figures are sequential displayed-value arithmetic on selected rows, not year-over-year comparisons, not non-GAAP measures, and not guidance; no causal driver is established by the arithmetic. Missing evidence: no balance-sheet totals, average loan balances, net interest margin, non-GAAP measures, guidance, segment detail, or management commentary on the drivers of the provision and nonaccrual movements; the extract cannot establish whether items are absent from the full filings. Because the selected evidence supports a genuinely two-sided credit and earnings picture without a source-backed driver, the research state is held for review rather than upgraded or invalidated.
